slots.title: 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.8%
slots.body:
10-year Treasury yield: 4.8% (snapshot dated Sept. 4, 2026).

2-year vs 10-year spread: 0.41 percentage points on the same curve.

CNBC reports that a sustained move above 4.8% on 10-year Treasurys is framed as creating meaningful pressure across other asset classes, with fiscal deficits and heavy issuance cited alongside corporate borrowing.

What level on the yield curve are you tracking ahead of the holiday-shortened week?

slots.title: August CPI still before mid-September Fed
slots.body:
Wall Street’s calendar this week centers on the August CPI report—the monthly measure of inflation in consumer prices.

Seeking Alpha notes market focus on that print as input to a September Fed decision, with one piece citing roughly 60% odds of a rate hike after strong payroll data.

Another piece describes Fed officials as data-dependent, with remarks from Governor Waller and Chair Warsh cited on how much CPI would need to soften to leave rates unchanged.

U.S. markets are closed Monday for Labour Day (Sept. 7).

Which inflation line item do you watch first in CPI?

$MSFT finished at 499.70, down 2.0%.

$CRM was down 2.0% to 259.23.

The S&P 500 ended at 7,718.60, off 0.4% (29.11 points).

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Sept. 6, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 finished at 7,718.60, down 29.11 points (-0.4%) after trading between 7,706.12 and 7,750.19.
The session kept the index below its 52-week high of 7,816.70 from the injected range data.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,506.99, down 0.3%, with an intraday band of 26,444.84 to 26,628.58.
Tech-heavy exposure showed the same mild risk-off tone as the broader large-cap benchmark.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.5%, ending at 53,414.25, a 271.86-point decline from the prior close.
That was the weakest major U.S. index print among the cap-weighted benchmarks in the feed.

The Russell 2000 was the outlier among U.S. indexes, up 0.2% to 2,975.65, while large-cap benchmarks were red.
Small caps in the feed held nearer their session high of 2,976.66 than the low at 2,951.04.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 1.5% to 14.53, from 14.32, with an intraday high of 14.58.
Implied equity volatility moved up slightly alongside the index declines.

Tesla closed at 354.08, down 5.9%, with volume of 65.0 million shares in the megacap set.
It was among the largest percentage declines in that group on the session.

Advanced Micro Devices rose 4.7% to 477.57, and ASML gained 4.2% to 1,714.88.
Oracle finished up 3.1% at 158.83.
Intel, among actives, closed up 4.5% at 95.80.

Apple fell 2.5% to 319.97, Microsoft dropped 2.0% to 499.70, and Salesforce declined 2.0% to 259.23.
Meta bucked that pattern with a 1.0% gain to 616.77.

Among liquid decliners, Guidewire fell 19.9% to 162.42, Lululemon lost 17.4% to 100.61, Fair Isaac dropped 16.7% to 932.26, and UiPath was down 16.6% to 15.19 in the active list.

Treasury snapshot data dated 2026-09-04 showed the 10-year yield at 4.8% and the 2s10s spread at 0.41 percentage points.
CNBC flagged fiscal and issuance pressure as markets watch whether long yields can hold below the 4.8% area.

Gold futures settled at 4,460.80, down 0.4%.
Brent crude was up 0.6% at 96.86, while the U.S. oil fund proxy (USO) closed at 141.96, down 0.1%.
The dollar-bullish fund proxy (UUP) rose 0.2% to 28.08.

Bitcoin quoted at 80,141.90, down 0.3% on the session.
Overseas, the Nikkei 225 rose 2.2%; the Hang Seng fell 1.1% to 25,357.50.

The economic calendar listed a U.S.-timed OPEC Meeting entry for 2026-09-06 with medium impact.
The earnings calendar in the feed carried no reported actuals for this close package.
